name: WebRAGent / GAE-Retriever (Multimodal Trajectory Retrieval and Retrieval-Augmented Web Agent; UATD + GAE-Bench)
venue: Core GAE-Retriever/UATD/GAE-Bench paper 'Universal Retrieval for Multimodal Trajectory Modeling' accepted as a poster at the Workshop on Computer-Use Agents @ ICML 2025 (WCUA 2025; OpenReview id wNFgL1c6It, Submission 37) and posted as arXiv:2506.22056 (cs.AI, 27 Jun 2025). The extended WebRAGent version 'WebRAGent: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multimodal Web Agent Planning' was submitted to ICLR 2026 (OpenReview id L1VPZFbAcu, Submission 17081, 19 Sept 2025) and REJECTED (Program Chairs decision 26 Jan 2026; scores 2/6/4/4). A further-revised version 'Learning Multimodal Trajectory Representations for Web Agent Planning' (OpenReview id XZputtLpjz, Mar 2026) exists. Task-specified venue label: OpenReview 2025 (GAE-Bench/UATD).

The ICLR 2026 WebRAGent submission adds Shengbo Cai, Lu Guangcheng, Zhiyong Wu and lists: Xuan Zhang, Shengbo Cai, Ziyan Jiang, Rui Meng, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Lu Guangcheng, Zhiyong Wu, Yanyi Shang, Dehan Kong. paper_url: https://openreview.net/forum?id=L1VPZFbAcu (ICLR 2026 WebRAGent submission; core paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.22056 and https://openreview.net/forum?id=wNFgL1c6It)
code_url: [uncertain] Reviewers repeatedly note the authors open-sourced code and resources to enhance reproducibility, but no official public GitHub/HuggingFace URL was verifiable from the OpenReview/arXiv pages at survey time (the github.com/dkruyt/WebRAgent repo is an unrelated project, not this work).
maintained_repo_url: [uncertain] No verifiable maintained leaderboard/repo URL found; UATD, GAE-Bench, GAE-Bench-lite and GAE-Bench-lite(mini) are released as datasets/benchmarks but the canonical hosting URL was not confirmable.
task_domain: web (GUI web-agent planning) plus multimodal information retrieval for agent trajectories. The retriever (GAE-Retriever) targets GUI agent trajectory retrieval across web/mobile/desktop sources; the downstream agent (WebRAGent) is a retrieval-augmented web-navigation agent.
problem_setting: Two coupled settings. (1) Offline supervised multimodal trajectory retrieval: given a query that can be text, a state (screenshot), a full trajectory, or a sub-trajectory, retrieve the matching state/trajectory/sub-trajectory from a candidate corpus; a VLM-based retriever is trained with contrastive learning on labeled positive pairs derived from human-annotated demonstrations (single-agent, supervision = labeled retrieval pairs from UATD/GAE-Bench-lite). (2) Interactive, single-agent retrieval-augmented web-agent planning: WebRAGent is a complete web agent (planner = GPT-4.1 in DOM mode, OpenAI computer-use-preview in Vision mode) that, at each step, retrieves step-level experience knowledge from a trajectory knowledge base via GAE-Retriever, reranks it with an LLM (GPT-4o), and conditions next-action prediction on the retrieved textual or visual exemplars. It runs in live, dynamic web environments (Online-Mind2Web), uses chain-of-thought reasoning, explicit history memory, and an LLM-as-judge reward module; the only difference between the non-retrieval baseline and WebRAGent is the presence/absence of the retrieval module.
what_is_retrieved: Multimodal GUI agent experience: states (screenshots), full trajectories, sub-trajectories/intervals, and step-level demonstrations (observation + action). In WebRAGent the retrieved unit is step-level experience knowledge from two knowledge bases: D_text (natural-language description of observation o~ + demonstration action a~ for the step) and D_vision (the step screenshot + structured action: operation type, target bounding box, input value). At the benchmark level, queries/targets are states, trajectories, or sub-trajectories.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (a curated demonstration/trajectory store). The retrievable store is the Unified Agent Trajectory Dataset (UATD)/GAE-Bench candidate set built offline from human-annotated demonstrations across five GUI sources; WebRAGent retrieves from this fixed trajectory knowledge base. It is NOT a growing/episodic memory the agent writes during deployment (no online write-back of new trajectories).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective. The retriever is trained and evaluated with InfoNCE contrastive loss and Recall@1/5/10; WebRAGent retrieves a top-k candidate set (Top-k=5 or 10 used on Online-Mind2Web) that is then LLM-reranked. There is no minimal-complete-set or variable-size precision-driven recommendation objective.
retrieval_unit: Heterogeneous multimodal units: single state s_i (a screenshot observation), full trajectory tau, or trajectory sub-sequence tau_{i:j} (ranging from a single state-action pair to the whole trajectory). In WebRAGent specifically, the retrieved unit is a step-level (observation, action) demonstration record (full-trajectory / sub-trajectory at training time; per-step exemplar at agent inference time).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced. UATD is built offline from five open-source GUI benchmarks (Mind2Web, AutoWebGLM, WebArena, WebLINX, GUIAct): 7,747 human-annotated demonstrations and 82,793 states. GAE-Bench (714,628 positive pairs via 12 extraction patterns) and GAE-Bench-lite (trajectories capped at <10 steps; 514,956 train / 21,805 in-domain / 27,139 out-of-domain, 574,222 candidates) are derived offline. The WebRAGent retrieval database is the UATD trajectory store. Frozen at deployment (no online growth).
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index over VLM embeddings (dense nearest-neighbor by maximum dot-product similarity). Candidate sets are organized by retrieval-target type (state / trajectory / interval) per data source (Table 5), and GAE-Bench has a typed task structure (6 tasks / 12 subtasks), but there is no graph or learned hierarchy in the retrieval index itself.
retriever_type: Learned dense multimodal retriever (VLM-as-retriever). GAE-Retriever is a contrastive embedding model built on VLM2Vec with a Qwen2-VL (Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct) backbone, embedding multimodal trajectories via the last-token final-layer representation. Used together with an LLM-based reranker (GPT-4o) in WebRAGent (hybrid retrieve-then-LLM-rerank).
retriever_learning_signal: Contrastive on similarity labels (downstream/task-supervised). GAE-Retriever is trained with the InfoNCE contrastive objective over positive retrieval pairs from GAE-Bench-lite, using large in-batch negatives enabled by GradCache. Positives include gold trajectories (q->tau_equiv from UATD ground truth) and silver trajectories (q->tau_sim, entity-substituted hard positives forcing procedural/skill-level invariance). Trained with LoRA (rank 8) on Qwen2-VL-Instruct, 16x H800 GPUs, accumulated batch size 2,048, 256 steps (~1,044 GPU hours), lr 5e-5. Not RL; not LM-feedback; not preference/Bradley-Terry.
query_construction: Query q-tilde is the raw input combined with a task-specific instruction (one of the 12 GAE-Bench instruction templates) plus a contextual trajectory description; the key/value follow a recursive grammar over states, actions, sub-trajectories, and full trajectories. In WebRAGent the query is the current state/context aligned to the agent's present step (state-conditioned, step-level retrieval). No automatic sub-query decomposition; entity substitution is used only to synthesize silver TRAINING pairs, not query-time expansion.
query_granularity: Both / two-level. At benchmark level queries span task-level (q->tau, q->s), state/step-level ((q,s)->s', (q,s)->tau), and trajectory-level ((q,tau)->tau', (q,tau)->s). In WebRAGent retrieval is step/state-level: step-level experience knowledge aligned with the current state is retrieved at each planning step.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative (per-step) in WebRAGent: retrieval is performed at each planning step using the current state, followed by LLM reranking, before the next action is predicted. (The retriever benchmark itself is a one-shot query->candidate task.) No uncertainty-triggered or learned-router gating; retrieval runs on a fixed per-step schedule.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (per-step, unconditional). WebRAGent issues a retrieval + rerank call at every planning step (one GAE-Retriever encoding + embedding retrieval + LLM rerank per step). There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated trigger.
reranking: Yes. An LLM-based reranker (GPT-4o) refines the GAE-Retriever Top-k candidates. The reranking prompt (Appendix E.2, Snippet 6) explicitly instructs the LLM to rank by (1) visual similarity of the screenshot, (2) consistency of UI elements/layout, and (3) semantic relevance of the task description. Reranking is the dominant inference-time cost (3.54 s/step without cache vs 0.39 s/step retrieval; reduced to ~0.0002 s/step with a two-level LLM-side cache, 9.24x speedup). Reported: with reranking, setting Top-k=5 improves R@1 by ~36% and Top-k=10 by ~54% on Online-Mind2Web.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank + compression. Post-retrieval processing = LLM-based reranking (cross-encoder-style relevance refinement) plus engineering optimizations (image compression / optimized encoding to reduce token consumption) before the retrieved exemplars are injected into the planner. No reason-in-documents distillation or decompose-then-recompose.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / case (exemplar) reuse. Reranked step-level textual (D_text) or visual (D_vision) knowledge is injected into the planner's prompt to guide chain-of-thought reasoning and next-action prediction. The planner prompt includes a 'Reuse Level Decision' mechanism instructing the agent to identify HIGH_LEVEL similarity (borrow intent/strategy) when element-level details do not match, so silver/analogous exemplars provide structural guidance rather than verbatim copying. No fine-tuning of the planner on retrieved items; everything is in-context. (At the retriever level, the learned embeddings are the artifact validated downstream.)
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved, retrieve-then-plan within an agent loop. At each step WebRAGent observes (DOM or screenshot), retrieves + reranks step-level experience knowledge aligned to the current state, then the planner (GPT-4.1 DOM mode / computer-use-preview Vision mode) performs long-horizon task decomposition and execution via CoT with explicit history memory and an LLM-as-judge reward. Not one-shot exemplars at plan time; not MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step (per planning step within the rollout): one retrieval+rerank+inject cycle per action decision. Not per-CoT-token or per-sentence.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mixed: both raw single demonstrations / state-action steps (low-level interaction details: operation type, target bounding box, value, screenshot) AND higher-level procedural/strategy guidance. The training design (silver trajectories) deliberately pushes the embedding to capture skill-level procedural similarity ('Search -> Filter -> Add-to-Cart') decoupled from specific parameters, and the planner is prompted to extract both high-level plans and low-level interaction patterns from retrieved exemplars.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface forms injected: (i) D_text - natural-language description of the observation plus the demonstration action for the step; (ii) D_vision - the step screenshot plus a structured action (operation, target bounding box, value). These are raw/lightly-structured per-step demonstration records, not distilled free-text strategies, executable programs, or latent tokens. (The retriever internally encodes trajectories as dense latent embeddings, but injected knowledge is human-readable text/image exemplars.)
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) LLM-based reranking of Top-k candidates filters/orders noisy retrievals by visual+layout+semantic relevance. (2) 'Reuse Level Decision' prompt mechanism instructs the agent to treat non-matching exemplars as HIGH_LEVEL structural guidance, preventing silver/analogous trajectories from acting as noisy supervision. (3) Silver-trajectory contrastive training teaches procedural invariance and improves OOD generalization (robustness to distribution shift). (4) Token selection (UI-connected RGB-space graph) suppresses redundant visual tokens. No explicit retriever-aware planner SFT or self-reflection relevance gate.
memory_type: Procedural / experience store (static demonstration knowledge base). The retrievable store is a fixed library of human-annotated GUI trajectories (UATD) treated as reusable procedural experience; not an episodic memory the agent grows, not a graph, not latent memory.
write_back: No. WebRAGent does not store its own newly generated trajectories/experiences back into the retrieval corpus; the trajectory knowledge base (UATD) is built offline and used read-only at deployment. (It does maintain a within-episode explicit history memory for the running task, but this is not written back to the retrievable store.)
online_growth: No. The retrieval store is frozen after offline induction from UATD; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
write_back_trigger: Never (for the retrievable trajectory store). No event causes a write into the retrieval corpus; new agent experiences are not consolidated. (Within a single episode the agent keeps a CoT/history memory and computes an LLM-as-judge reward score per step, but neither is persisted as a new retrievable case.)
failure_experience_usage: Success-only / demonstration-based. The retrieval corpus consists of human-annotated successful demonstrations; failed agent trajectories are not stored or contrastively retrieved. The step-level LLM-as-judge reward (scores from {1,3,7,9,10}; categories doing/finished/loop) steers the running agent (e.g., reset-and-recover on loops) but is not used to mine or store failure cases for retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (static store). Stored entries are not mutated after offline construction (no append/dedup/merge/refine/forget at deployment); the corpus is fixed.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partial: case-SELECTION is via a LEARNED dense retriever (GAE-Retriever, contrastively trained VLM embeddings) plus an LLM reranker, rather than an off-the-shelf fixed similarity model. However retrieval is NOT an RL- or value-optimized sequential policy (no M-MDP / soft Q-learning); it is a learned-embedding top-k + LLM rerank.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Cross-framework transfer demonstrated (not shared private memory). GAE-Retriever is shown to be plug-and-play: integrated into the SeeAct agent framework it yields an 8-10% success-rate gain (SeeAct 49.0% -> +D_text 57.0% -> +D_vision 59.0% on the 100-task Online-Mind2Web subset), demonstrating that the retrieved trajectory knowledge transfers across heterogeneous agent frameworks. The retrieval corpus itself is a shared static resource, not per-agent private growing memory.
benchmarks: Retrieval evaluation: GAE-Bench / GAE-Bench-lite over five sources - Mind2Web, AutoWebGLM, WebArena, WebLINX, GUIAct (Recall@1/5/10; in-domain and out-of-domain splits). Downstream web-agent evaluation: Online-Mind2Web (a representative 100-task subset selected via two-stage stratified sampling from the original set, balanced across websites/categories and easy/medium/hard difficulty). SeeAct cross-framework study also on the 100-task Online-Mind2Web subset.
benchmark_family: web (Mind2Web / WebArena / WebLINX / GUIAct / AutoWebGLM for offline trajectory retrieval; Online-Mind2Web for the live downstream agent). Plus a new multimodal-retrieval benchmark family introduced by the paper itself (GAE-Bench).
baselines: Retrieval baselines (zero-shot, three groups): (1) Multimodal backbone models - Qwen2-VL-2B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B; (2) Multimodal retrieval models - LamRA-Ret, ColQwen2-v1.0, GME-Qwen2VL-2B, UniSE-MLLM, VLM2Vec-Qwen2VL-2B, VLM2Vec-V2.2 (strongest baseline); (3) Multimodal trajectory/GUI planning models - UGround-V1-2B, ShowUI-2B, UI-TARS-2B-SFT, TongUI-3B. Downstream (WebRAGent): non-retrieval agent with the SAME planner (GPT-4.1 DOM / computer-use-preview Vision), same observation/action/reward/prompts, differing only by the retrieval module; SeeAct (added in rebuttal) as a cross-framework baseline (+/- retrieval). Also text-only retrieval (q->tau) vs multimodal retrieval comparison (Appendix D.5).
key_metrics: Retrieval: Recall@1/5/10. Downstream web agent: task Success Rate (%) on Online-Mind2Web, broken down by Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty. Efficiency: seconds/step for retrieval vs reranking vs total, and cache speedup. Reranking effect: relative R@1 improvement at Top-k=5 / Top-k=10.
headline_result: WebRAGent improves web-agent task Success Rate by over 15% (reported as 15-22%, and 16-22% in the later revision) versus the non-retrieval baseline on the 100-task Online-Mind2Web subset, using identical planners (GPT-4.1 DOM / computer-use-preview Vision) and differing only in the retrieval module. For the retriever itself, GAE-Retriever surpasses all baselines on every dataset, with Recall@1 consistently >10.0; e.g., Recall@10 of 76.3 on AutoWebGLM and 67.9 on GUIAct, improving Recall@1 over the strongest baseline VLM2Vec-V2.2 by up to 7.1 points (GUIAct) / 6.4 points (AutoWebGLM), with an average +10.22-point improvement across five datasets over the best baseline (up to +12.9 Recall@1 per the conclusion).
ablations: (1) Cross-framework plug-and-play (SeeAct, 100-task Online-Mind2Web): SeeAct 49.0% -> +D_text 57.0% -> +D_vision 59.0% (8-10% gain), with visual knowledge best on Medium (60.52%) and Hard (25.00%) tasks. (2) Textual vs visual RAG: both effective; visual exemplars help more on fine-grained Medium/Hard operations. (3) Multimodal vs text-only retrieval (Appendix D.5, Table 11): multimodal/state-conditioned retrieval beats text-only q->tau by ~22%. (4) Reranking Top-k effect on Online-Mind2Web: Top-k=5 improves R@1 by ~36%, Top-k=10 by ~54%. (5) Inference efficiency (Appendix D.7, RTX A6000): retrieval 0.39 s/step vs reranking 3.54 s/step; with two-level LLM cache total drops to 0.383 s/step (9.24x speedup), ~10% added latency/step. (6) Retriever per-task analysis: semantic tasks (q->tau, q->s) easiest; (q,tau)->tau' and (q,s)->tau hardest; GAE-Retriever sometimes higher OOD than IND, indicating generalizable representations. (7) Token Selection vs alternatives (Appendix D.8). Open issue raised by reviewers: no isolated ablation separating the silver-data contribution.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@1/5/10, in-domain and out-of-domain, per task/subtask) are reported separately from the end-to-end web-agent Success Rate on Online-Mind2Web, explicitly linking better trajectory representations to better downstream agent performance.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mixed. Downstream metric is outcome-level task Success Rate, but reported by difficulty stratum (Easy/Medium/Hard) and accompanied by qualitative step-level case studies (Appendix F) marking where retrieved knowledge is cited at each critical step, plus a step-level LLM-as-judge reward signal and per-step latency analysis. Retrieval side reports ranking-quality (process) metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported. Retrieval augmentation adds ~10% latency per step. Per-step cost: retrieval 0.3877 s, reranking 3.5374 s, total 3.9251 s without cache; with a two-level LLM-side cache + compressed image encoding, total 0.3830 s/step (9.24x speedup), reranking near-negligible on cache hits. Training cost: 16x NVIDIA H800, LoRA rank 8, accumulated batch 2,048, 256 steps, ~1,044 GPU hours. The 15-22% success gain is argued to justify the modest added retrieval cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Reranked-then-truncated fixed-k: GAE-Retriever returns Top-k candidates (Top-k=5 or 10 on Online-Mind2Web) which the LLM reranker refines; the top reranked step-level exemplar(s) (textual or visual) are injected into the planner prompt. Trajectory length capped at <10 steps in GAE-Bench-lite to fit VLM context windows; token selection further reduces visual tokens to keep high-resolution multi-image trajectories within budget. No adaptive/precision-driven variable-k.
benchmark_construction_and_size: UATD: 7,747 human-annotated demonstrations and 82,793 states unified from five GUI sources (Mind2Web 1,468 tasks/9,621 states; AutoWebGLM 140/620; WebArena 201/1,221; WebLINX 485/6,882; GUIAct 5,453/64,449); screenshots kept at original resolution, target elements as bounding boxes, missing screenshots rendered via gpt-4o-mini HTML completion + Playwright, state descriptions auto-annotated (gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18). GAE-Bench: 714,628 positive retrieval pairs from 12 extraction patterns over 6 retrieval task types (text-to-state, text-to-trajectory, state-to-state, state-to-trajectory, trajectory-to-state, trajectory-to-trajectory). GAE-Bench-lite (<10-step trajectories): 514,956 train / 21,805 in-domain / 27,139 out-of-domain, 574,222 candidates; plus a GAE-Bench-lite(mini) candidate partition. Silver trajectories built via NER -> entity-type-preserving substitution -> query rewrite. Answer verifiability: ground-truth positive pairs are derived from human demonstrations (gold) plus synthesized silver positives. Difficulty signal: even the strongest GAE-Retriever reaches Recall@1 only ~10-26 and the hardest subtasks ((q,tau)->tau', (q,s)->tau) remain low.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (learned dense multimodal retrieval + LLM rerank of past demonstrations), Reuse: yes (retrieved step-level exemplars injected into the planner, with an explicit Reuse-Level decision for high-level vs element-level adaptation), Revise: partial (the planner adapts/borrows strategy from analogous exemplars and an LLM-as-judge reward triggers reset-and-recover, but there is no formal per-case revise-and-store step), Retain: no (no write-back of new cases into the corpus)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself as multimodal trajectory representation learning / retrieval-augmented generation for web agents; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes Retrieve/Reuse mechanisms (and references skill abstraction, Agent Workflow Memory, SkillWeaver, RaDA, Synapse) under a RAG/representation-learning framing.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool/API retrieval method; retrieved items are GUI trajectory states/steps, not tool documents).
index_content_separation: Partial: GAE-Retriever produces a lightweight dense embedding index for fast nearest-neighbor retrieval, after which heavier content (full screenshots + structured actions / textual descriptions) is loaded and LLM-reranked. Token selection separates salient UI tokens from redundant background, and image compression/two-level caching are used to manage on-demand heavy-content loading. There is no formal progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content protocol.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (the trajectory store is a static internally-managed corpus, not a live tool registry with MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful/function-calling sync).
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation of retrieved exemplars: the planner reuses retrieved step-level demonstrations as guidance, applying a 'Reuse Level Decision' (HIGH_LEVEL strategy borrowing vs element-level reuse) so that analogous/silver trajectories provide structural/procedural guidance rather than verbatim solutions; an LLM-as-judge reward enables execution-feedback-driven recovery (reset-and-recover) within the episode. No RL reuse-finetuning of the planner.
builds_on: VLM2Vec (Jiang et al., 2025; Qwen2-VL backbone embedding model) extended to trajectory contrastive learning; GradCache (Gao et al., 2021) for large-batch contrastive training under memory limits; token selection via UI-connected RGB-space graph (inspired by Raposo et al. 2024 mixture-of-depths and ShowUI / Lin et al. 2024a); AGUVIS (Xu et al., 2024) for screenshot-as-observation unified GUI formulation; ShowUI action schema for the unified action space; source datasets Mind2Web, AutoWebGLM, WebArena, WebLINX, GUIAct; Online-Mind2Web for live evaluation; SeeAct (Zheng et al. 2024) as the cross-framework integration target. Conceptually relates to RaDA (Kim et al. 2024), Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024), Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al. 2024c), SkillWeaver (Zheng et al. 2025), and retrieval-augmented RL (Goyal et al. 2022).
contrasts_with: CLIP-based / single-image multimodal retrievers (CLIP, BLIP, composed video retrieval) - unsuitable for long multi-image high-resolution (~1000x1000) GUI trajectories; text/DOM-only trajectory retrieval (RaDA matching textual trajectory descriptions, Synapse matching DOM/HTML states) - argued to miss visual semantics (layout, icon status, rendering); end-to-end pure-vision GUI agents such as AGUVIS that aggregate trajectories to train action policies (next-action labels) rather than a trajectory RETRIEVER; and screenshot-only retrievers (UniSE-MLLM) which underperform. Also positioned as introducing a 'representation layer' missing from reactive-generation GUI agents.
lineage: Group C (RAG + planning) with strong overlap into retrieval-augmented web-agent and trajectory/experience-retrieval lines (B/D). It advances the RaDA -> Synapse -> Agent-Workflow-Memory line of retrieval-augmented web-agent planning by (a) introducing the Multimodal Trajectory Retrieval task and the UATD/GAE-Bench infrastructure, (b) training the first VLM-based multimodal trajectory retriever (GAE-Retriever) with token selection + GradCache, and (c) wrapping it in WebRAGent, a DOM+vision retrieval-augmented web agent validated on Online-Mind2Web. Distinctive emphasis: a static, supervised, learned multimodal trajectory-retrieval layer (vs growing episodic memory) feeding per-step LLM-reranked exemplars to a strong web-agent planner.
